text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong proposes increasing number of members of parliament who can be elected from multi-member districts.
- Government proposes changes to the workings of the elected president which will affect his veto and appointment powers.
- Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto pledges wide-ranging reforms.
- Singapore bus driver stops bus to chase purse-snatcher.
- Pidemco Land revives plans to integrate its Orchard Road properties into a shopping precinct with Centrepoint Properties flagship building.
- Pidemco Land aims for 10 to 15 percent growth in annual profits and wants to expand its Singapore $4.3 billion current asset base over the next five years.

- The number of shares traded on the Stock Exchange of Singapore last month plunges 61 percent to 1.8 billion, the second consecutive month in which turnover shrunk by more than half the volume traded over the same period last year.
- Hongkong-listed garmet exporter Easyknit International Holdings public share offer 70 percent undersubscribed, making it first secondary listing in Singapore to draw such a disappointing response.
- Singapore Confederation of Industries building industrial park within Qingdao Hi-Tech Industrial Park in China and expects investment commitments worth S$400-S$500 million from Singapore investors.
- Movements in regional currencies driven on Monday by politics or politicians' remarks.
- Hongkong-listed property developer and metal trader Burwill Holdings reports 42 percent drop in net earnings to Hongkong $75.3 million.
- Scotts Holdings details S$3.2 million owed by director-related companies, and directors tell Business Times the have arranged for amount to be paid by October 14.
- Singapore Bus Service through subsidiary jointly developing 130,000 sq metre industrial site in Tuas South with Technology Parks and Lend Lease Asia.
- Hongkong-based electronics company IDT International Ltd will sell shares in it its liquid-crystal display products division for a separate listing in Singapore.
